transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Um... I guess it's just... I can't really keep my words in a straight line anymore. 

Like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift, and... I don't know. I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or... patient charts. I can just see everyone getting lost when I talk to them. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Along with this jumping around in your speech, have you also noticed feeling unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual over the same period?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really felt energetic or anything like that. I just sleep when I can. So... no.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or feeling that people are watching or plotting against you?

Um... no voices or anything. But... I don't know. I know the supervisors at work are watching me. Through the unit cameras. They keep changing my shifts around... and people tell me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know they're doing it to see if I'm unsafe. So... yeah. Just that.
Have you been using cocaine or any other stimulant drugs recently, and if so, how often?
No. I don't... I don't use anything like that. Just coffee. That's it.

How long have you been noticing this trouble keeping your thoughts organized and the feeling that you're being watched by your supervisors—has this been going on for weeks, or longer, like several months?

Um... it's been a while. Longer than a few months. I guess... maybe a year and a half? About a year and five months. It all started when they stopped giving me steady day shifts. They put me on rotating nights... and making me do overtime. That's when I noticed it.
Over this past year and a half, have you noticed your work performance, relationships, or ability to take care of daily responsibilities getting worse because of these experiences?

Yeah... I guess so. Work's been hard. I... I have to ask the other aides to check my rounds. And my charting. Just to make sure I didn't mess up. 

And at home... I don't know. I haven't been paying my bills on time. My apartment's a mess. I haven't really talked to anyone... friends, I mean. 

It just... it got to the point where employee health sent me to the ER. Because... I told them I was thinking about ending it. So... yeah. It's been bad.
Over this past year and a half, have you noticed periods of feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah... I guess. Just... heavy, mostly. And empty. Pretty much every day, right from when I wake up. 

And um... after my shifts... I don't know. I just sit in my car for a long time. Sometimes I end up... crying in the parking lot before I can even pull myself together to drive home. So... yeah. Most days.

Thinking back over this year and a half, were there any stretches of time when you weren't feeling down, empty, or tearful, but you still believed your supervisors were watching or plotting against you?

Um... yeah. There was a time. A few weeks, maybe. I wasn't... I didn't feel as heavy. The crying stopped for a bit. 

But I still... I still knew they were watching. The cameras. I still had to be careful at work. Even when I wasn't feeling so down... I still had to watch my back.
Out of the entire year and a half, would you say the down, empty, tearful periods have been present most of the time, with that one symptom-free stretch of a few weeks being the exception?
Yeah... mostly. The heavy feeling... it's just kind of always there. Even when the camera stuff wasn't as bad, or my thoughts weren't so messy... I still felt empty. So, yeah... most of the time.
